title: 3.2 PHYSICAL PROPERTIES
summary: Gas Pipeline Compression and Corrosion and Liquid Dropout Risk is a pressure differential like a vacuum on one side and high pressure on the other. Distillation, distillation as a Separation Method, energy Cost of Distillation at Scale, physical vs. chemical changes, gas compression and expansion Thermodynamics, and Melting Point and Boiling Point as Separation Tools each describe how substances change phase and how those transitions can be exploited or become hazards. Vapor-Compression Cooling Cycle (Air Conditioning and Refrigeration) and Pipeline Phase-Change Hazards extend this to practical systems, showing how phase changes are engineered for cooling or must be guarded against in transit. Phase (State of Matter) and Its Trading Relevance and Gas Pressure, Volume, and Temperature Interdependence (Ideal Gas Law) tie these physical principles back to how fuels are handled, transported, and traded.
